nodes.title: Definition of Precipitation
nodes.outcome: Define precipitation and list its different forms including rain, snow, and hail.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Trace the Water Cycle
nodes.outcome: Trace the continuous movement of water from Earth's surface to the atmosphere and back through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, and precipitation.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Diagram the Water Cycle
nodes.outcome: Draw and label a schematic diagram representing the major stages of the natural water cycle.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Groundwater and Water Table
nodes.outcome: Define groundwater and the water table as the upper limit of the water-saturated underground layer.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Infiltration
nodes.outcome: Define infiltration as the process of water seeping through soil into the ground.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Definition of Aquifer
nodes.outcome: Identify an aquifer as the underground reservoir of water stored between layers of hard rock below the water table.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Rainwater Harvesting Techniques
nodes.outcome: Describe rooftop and open-ground rainwater harvesting methods used to recharge groundwater.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Evaluate Water Conservation
nodes.outcome: Evaluate community and domestic practices that prevent water wastage and promote sustainable groundwater replenishment.

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Mixture
nodes.outcome: Define a mixture as a combination of two or more substances that retain their individual properties

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Classify Mixture Components
nodes.outcome: Classify components of a mixture into useful components, non-useful components, and harmful impurities

nodes.title: State Reasons for Separation
nodes.outcome: List three primary purposes of separation: removing harmful impurities, separating non-useful components, and obtaining pure useful components

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Match Separation Examples to Purpose
nodes.outcome: Match daily examples like churning butter, straining tea leaves, and picking stones from rice to their specific separation purpose

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Handpicking
nodes.outcome: Describe handpicking as a method of manually picking out larger impurities from a mixture based on visible differences in size, shape, or colour

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Handpicking Conditions
nodes.outcome: Identify conditions where handpicking is practical: small quantity of mixture, low concentration of impurities, and noticeable difference in size/appearance

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Threshing
nodes.outcome: Describe threshing as the process of beating stalks to free grain seeds using manual beating, bullocks, or machines

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Winnowing
nodes.outcome: Describe winnowing as a method used to separate heavier grain seeds from lighter husk using blowing wind or air

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Winnowing Principle
nodes.outcome: Explain how difference in mass/weight of solid particles causes heavier particles to drop vertically and lighter particles to blow away during winnowing

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Sieving
nodes.outcome: Describe sieving as a method of passing a dry mixture through a mesh where fine particles pass through holes and larger particles remain on the sieve

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Sieve Mesh Selection
nodes.outcome: Explain why mesh/pore size of a sieve must be selected intermediate to the sizes of the two components being separated

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Select Dry Separation Method
nodes.outcome: Select the appropriate dry separation method (handpicking, threshing, winnowing, or sieving) for a given novel solid mixture based on particle properties

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Magnetic Separation
nodes.outcome: Identify magnetic separation as a method to separate magnetic components (like iron pins or filings) from non-magnetic dry mixtures using a magnet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Sedimentation
nodes.outcome: Define sedimentation as the process in which heavier insoluble solid particles in a liquid mixture settle down at the bottom when left undisturbed

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Decantation
nodes.outcome: Define decantation as the process of carefully pouring off the clear upper liquid layer without disturbing the settled sediment at the bottom

nodes.title: Apply Decantation to Immiscible Liquids
nodes.outcome: Apply decantation to separate two immiscible liquids (such as oil and water) based on difference in layer formation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Filtration
nodes.outcome: Define filtration as the process of passing a liquid-solid mixture through a porous medium to retain fine insoluble solid particles while allowing liquid to pass

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Distinguish Filtrate and Residue
nodes.outcome: Distinguish between filtrate (the clear liquid passing through the filter) and residue (the solid trapped on the filter)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Compare Decantation and Filtration
nodes.outcome: Compare decantation and filtration in terms of clarity of separated liquid and efficiency in removing ultra-fine suspended particles

nodes.outcome: Predict the effect of heating on a saturated solution in allowing additional solute to dissolve

nodes.title: Compare Stimulus Responses
nodes.outcome: Compare the speed and mechanisms of response to external stimuli between plants and animals

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Reproduction

nodes.title: Classify Living and Non-Living
nodes.outcome: Classify objects as living, non-living, or dead by evaluating the presence of all life characteristics

nodes.title: Define Habitat and Basic Needs
nodes.outcome: Define a habitat as the natural dwelling place providing food, water, air, and shelter for an organism

nodes.title: Classify Biotic and Abiotic Factors
nodes.outcome: Classify habitat components into biotic factors (living organisms) and abiotic factors (soil, water, air, temperature, sunlight)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Differentiate Habitat Types
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between terrestrial habitats (deserts, mountains, grasslands) and aquatic habitats (ponds, lakes, rivers, oceans)

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Biotic-Abiotic Interactions
nodes.outcome: Explain how abiotic factors like sunlight, moisture, and temperature influence the survival and distribution of biotic organisms

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Define Adaptation
nodes.outcome: Define adaptation as specific structural, physiological, or behavioural traits that enable an organism to survive in its habitat

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Distinguish Adaptation from Acclimatisation
nodes.outcome: Distinguish long-term evolutionary adaptations from short-term bodily adjustments (acclimatisation)

nodes.subject: Science

nodes.outcome: Identify camel structural adaptations including long legs, concentrated urine, dry dung, lack of sweat, and wide padded feet

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Desert Plant Adaptations

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Fish Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Identify structural adaptations of fish for underwater living including a streamlined body, gills for dissolved oxygen, fins, and slippery scales

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Aquatic Plant Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Identify adaptations of aquatic plants including flexible stems, air cavities for buoyancy, reduced root systems, and waxy coatings

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Mountain Tree Adaptations
nodes.outcome: Explain how conical shape, sloping branches, and needle-like leaves help mountain trees shed snow and resist wind

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Mountain Animal Adaptations

nodes.title: Compare Grassland Predator and Prey Adaptations

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Describe Forest Habitat and Biodiversity Support

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Atmospheric Gas Balance by Forests

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Forest Influence on Water Cycle

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Forest Role in Flood Control and Infiltration

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Identify Causes of Soil Erosion
nodes.outcome: Identify human and natural activities that accelerate soil erosion, including deforestation, overgrazing, and unscientific farming

nodes.title: List Causes of Air Pollution

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: List Causes of Water Pollution
nodes.outcome: List major causes of water pollution including domestic sewage discharge, industrial effluent release, and agricultural runoff

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Explain Impacts of Deforestation
nodes.outcome: Explain the multi-dimensional impacts of deforestation on rainfall, global temperature, biodiversity loss, and soil degradation

nodes.subject: Science
nodes.title: Suggest Soil Conservation Methods

nodes.title: Define Celestial Objects

nodes.title: Fixed Position of Pole Star

nodes.title: Components of Solar System

nodes.title: Order Planets by Distance

nodes.title: Inner vs Outer Planets
nodes.outcome: Differentiate between inner rocky planets and outer gaseous planets by composition and location

nodes.title: Orbital Period and Distance
